summary: Independent review reproduced the remaining post-lock dispatch race on the exact recorded base and verified the exact candidate commit. The base already rejects completed futures at group entry and between per-request encodes, but a request completed while waiting for encode_dispatch_lock was still broadcast and passed to batch_encode. Candidate eb9138b re-filters under the lock and rebuilds the request list before broadcast. Candidate regressions and independent adversarial cases confirm that timed-out, cancelled, or completed work reaches neither broadcast nor encoder while live work completes. This is a full fix for the original issue in the current base context, not merely test hardening.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before comparison on 358c163: dequeue timeout and per-request completion races passed, while the post-lock race failed because batch_encode received ['completed', 'live']. Raw output: raw/base-focused.txt
Exact candidate eb9138b: all three candidate regressions passed using actual PendingRequest and EncoderScheduler dispatch paths; 3 passed. Raw output: raw/candidate-focused.txt

Independent candidate cases: decoded two-socket broadcast payloads contained only the live request after mixed cancellation/completion; an all-abandoned post-lock batch produced no broadcast or encoder call; and a request cancelled while an earlier per-request encode blocked was skipped while the later live request completed. 3 passed. Retained test and output: raw/adversarial_test.py and raw/candidate-adversarial.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: The reported defect is a Python asyncio scheduler race and the issue explicitly identifies the scheduler seam as CPU-reproducible. Tests exercised production PendingRequest, worker/dispatch methods, encode_dispatch_lock, sock_send call sites, batch_encode, and per-request encode. No model or GPU numerical claim was made.

remaining_limitations: No native source changed, repository-environment.json reports native=null and wheel=null, so no native rebuild was applicable. The imported runtime source was confirmed as /job/repo/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encoder/runtime.py. No real tensor-parallel processes, model weights, HTTP transport, or GPU were used; broadcast exclusion was verified at the production sock_send boundary with decoded payloads, not across a distributed collective. These architecture limitations do not leave a counterexample to the original Python scheduler contract.
